summary:
ADVERSARIAL CHECK OF THE COSTS AND TAX AUDIT FOR VARIANT 5 ("Les deux"). My scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-snt-2b-adam-cieniewicz/4246b01c-1857-5934-aed2-b3eb85d88a07/scratchpad/audit/verif_couts/ (cash_shortfall.py, cash_shortfall_corrected.csv, total_drag_corrected.csv, plus fresh copies of the pysystemtrade config files ic.csv and sc.csv). No project file was modified. I used the whole web-search budget (200 calls), so some secondary items stay unverifiable.

Most commission, fee and tax figures check out:
- IBKR commissions: US $0.85/0.65/0.45/0.25, Eurex €0.90 (€2.00 fixed), FDAX/FDXM/FDXS fees, OSE ¥230, ASX A$3.55.
- Other IBKR items: the $10 US futures data bundle waived at $30 of commissions, the $500 equity minimum for market data, T-bill commission 0.002% (min $5), and the weekly 2FA re-login.
- Other providers: Saxo $3/€3, Norgate $270, QuantConnect $84/month, Hetzner €5.49 + €0.50, IB01 TER 0.07%, XEON 0.10%.
- Rates: Fed range 3.75–4.00 after 16 Sep 2026, ECB deposit rate 2.50% from 16 Sep 2026, T-bill 4.00% (and the 2.73% / 1.49% averages).
- French tax: PFU 31.4% (12.8 + 18.6, CSG 9.2→10.6%), applying to capital gains from 2025 income and to investment income from 1 Jan 2026; the 17.2% exclusions; CDHR; article 150 ter with 10-year carry-forward against same-nature gains; boxes 3VG/3VH and form 2074-CMV; €1,500 / €10,000 penalty per undeclared account; iMGP DBi TER 0.75%.
- Data: the pysystemtrade files the previous agent used are identical to today's GitHub versions. The backtest cost of 2.38%/yr (1990–2026) and 2.31%/yr (2023-07→2026-07) reproduces from the cache. The QS1 → GASOILINE mis-mapping in carry_inputs_info is real.

MAIN CORRECTION — cash interest. The previous model pays interest on all cash at IBKR, including the futures margin. IBKR's "Margin Interest Calculations" page says no interest is paid on commodity-segment balances, which is where futures margin sits. So the margin earns nothing: about 23% of capital on average for v5, up to 40% at the 95th percentile. This adds about 0.23 × 3.36% ≈ 0.77 point/yr to the shortfall versus the T-bill for accounts of $100k or more.

Corrected USD shortfall, policy of 50% of capital in T-bills:

| Capital | Previous | Corrected |
|---|---|---|
| $100k | 0.67 % | 1.44 % |
| $250k | 0.46 % | 1.24 % |
| $500k | 0.40 % | 1.17 % |
| $1M | 0.36 % | 1.14 % |
| $5M | 0.34 % | 1.11 % |

All cash at IBKR: 1.42–1.75 % instead of 0.65–0.98 %. With margin at 40% of capital it rises to about 1.7–2.0 %.

Corrected total drag versus the backtest (lean data, 50% T-bills, +0.5% extra variable cost):

| Capital | Previous | Corrected |
|---|---|---|
| $25k | 6.4 % | 6.5 % |
| $50k | 4.0 % | 4.4 % |
| $100k | 2.2 % | 2.9 % |
| $250k | 1.4 % | 2.1 % |
| $500k | 1.1 % | 1.9 % |
| $1M | 0.96 % | 1.74 % |
| $2M | 0.90 % | 1.67 % |
| $5M | 0.86 % | 1.63 % |

For a EUR investor, the shortfall versus €STR goes from about 0.28% to about 0.72% at $1M or more.

Other corrections:
1. The "5% of the balance if €50k or more" penalty for an undeclared foreign account is wrong. The Conseil constitutionnel struck it down (decision 2016-554 QPC, 22 July 2016). The penalty is €1,500 per account per year, or €10,000 for a non-cooperative state.
2. The IBKR account is declared on form 3916, which is part of the combined cerfa "3916-3916-bis". The 3916-bis part is for crypto (digital-asset) accounts. That part matters for the user's bitcoin if it sits on a foreign exchange.
3. BNC requalification risk: the legal basis is article 92-2-5° CGI (BOI-BNC-SECT-50). The previous agent left out what it means in practice:
   - profits taxed at the progressive income-tax scale plus social charges, not the PFU;
   - losses usable only against same-nature BNC profits, for 6 years, so not against QQQ gains.
4. The NFA fee is $0.01 per side until 30 June 2027 ($0.02 after), not $0.02 now.
5. ICE real-time data costs more than stated. AMP's non-professional rates (June 2026) are ICE US $148, ICE Europe commodities $161 and financials $139. ICE's own 2026 PDF lists energy at $144, not $131. The full real-time budget is therefore about $750/yr too low. This is irrelevant for a daily system that uses delayed ICE data.
6. The Nikkei 225 large contract costs about ¥410 all-in at IBKR (¥280 commission + ¥110 exchange + ¥20 clearing), against ¥330 assumed. Negligible.
7. Hetzner prices exclude VAT (about €7.19/month with 20% VAT). Negligible.
8. The after-tax simulation uses the USD T-bill as the cash rate for a EUR investor and keeps the old cash-interest model, so the after-tax CAGRs are somewhat overstated.

Still valid:
- Variable costs are realistic once the strategy is fully replicated. I verified the inputs; I did not re-run the model.
- Below about $1–2M the strategy cannot be replicated with real contracts.
- After-tax return is roughly 0.56–0.69 × pre-tax.

Overall: for an account of $1M or more, the realistic pre-tax drag versus the backtest is about 1.6–1.8%/yr, roughly double the previous 0.9%, before about a third goes to tax.

Consequences the previous agent left out: progressive income-tax scale (not PFU) plus social charges; losses NOT deductible from global income, only against same-nature (habitual IFT) profits of the same year and the following 6 years (not 10, and not against QQQ capital gains).

However: it uses the USD T-bill as cash for a EUR investor, inherits the over-generous cash-interest model, pays tax at year-end instead of Sep N+1 (slightly pessimistic), and ignores the BNC scenario. problems: MAJOR: the cash-interest model (assemble.py ib_interest) pays IBKR interest on all cash, including futures margin. IBKR pays no interest on commodity-segment balances (margin-calculation-details page). The cash shortfall vs the T-bill is understated by about 0.23 × 3.36 ≈ 0.77 point/yr for accounts of $100k or more (more at higher margin). Total drag at $1M is about 1.74 %/yr, not 0.96; at $5M about 1.63, not 0.86 (verif_couts/total_drag_corrected.csv).

REFUTED: the '5 % of the balance if ≥ €50k' penalty for undeclared foreign accounts was struck down by Conseil constitutionnel decision 2016-554 QPC (22 Jul 2016). Remove it; the penalty is €1,500 (or €10,000) per account per year.

Form naming: the IBKR account goes on form 3916 (part of the combined cerfa 3916-3916-bis). 3916-bis is the crypto-account part, which is relevant to the user's bitcoin if it is held on a foreign exchange.

BNC requalification is under-specified. Basis is art. 92-2-5° CGI. Consequences: progressive scale instead of PFU, and losses only against same-nature BNC profits for 6 years (not 10, and not against QQQ gains). This should be stated because thousands of automated trades make it a real scenario.

ICE real-time data fees understated. Non-professional rates (AMP, June 2026) are ICE US $148, ICE Europe commodities $161 and financials $139; ICE's 2026 PDF lists energy at $144, not $131. The full real-time budget is about $750–900/yr higher. Low impact for a daily system using delayed data.
NFA fee is $0.01 per side until 30 Jun 2027, not $0.02 (negligible).
